summary: An explicit generic affine-lineprior in a nontrivialSO2GaussianMRA model meetsCor3.1andhassecondmomentinjectivity, yet firstmoment recovery hasMSE proportional to sigma^2/n. ThereforeCor4.3's unconditional n/sigma^4 minimalnecessity isfalse. Maintransversality conclusions notrefuted.

problems.title: Second-moment sufficiency is not a universal necessary sample rate

source_claim.locator: Corollary4.3 PDF16–17 (2780–2781); model4.5 and Cor3.1 PDF10
source_claim.text: Under the stated prior conditions, the minimal necessary observation growth is n/sigma^4 ->infinity regardless of algorithm.

assumptions: G=SO(2) acts onV=R2 directsumR2 by(z,w)->(z,Rtheta w); Haar rotations and iid N(0,sigma^2 I) noise
Known generic affine line p+t u, M1, det(p0,u0)!=0, K>2M

check.type: exact analytical proof, calculation, or literal source comparison
steps: First fixed-coordinate block of second moment is(p0+t u0)(p0+t u0)^T; equality implies same vector up tosign.
det(p0,u0)!=0 excludes negative-sign equality at distinct t, proving actual second-moment injectivity.
First moment is(p0+t u0,0), already identifyingt.
Estimator t_hat=u0^T(ybar0-p0)/||u0||^2 has exactMSE sigma^2/(n||u0||^2).
Full signal estimator hasMSE ||u||^2 sigma^2/(n||u0||^2).
n=ceil(sigma^3) givesMSE->0 but n/sigma^4->0; x_t=(t,1,t,1) gives2sigma^2/n.
Nonzero determinant is open generic, so this is not only an exceptional prior.
check.result: Explicit consistent estimator contradicts unconditional minimal necessary rate.

counterevidence: Deterministic transversality and Cor3.1 identifiability hold in the witness.
Cor4.2 states a sufficient cryo-EM rate and is not refuted.

impact.dependency: Advertised information-theoretic application infers lowest identifying moment from a merely sufficient moment.
impact.scope: Major applies to unconditional necessity/minimality in Cor4.3, not whole-paper failure.

correction.statement: State second-moment sufficiency, or impose and establish first-moment nonidentifiability plus required statistical lower-bound assumptions.
correction.verification: Exact risk calculation shows why the missing first-moment distinction matters.
correction.limits: No complete minimax replacement theorem or general conditioning result proved.

problems.title: Joint semi-algebraicity missing from general action hypothesis

check.type: exact analytical proof, calculation, or literal source comparison
steps: Every fixedtheta map is invertible linear and semi-algebraic.
Between e1 and(0,t), the collision equation is t=exp(theta).
This branch is not semi-algebraic.
check.result: Pointwise action condition does not imply joint incidence property.
